components.name: Typography
components.element: div, h1, h2, p, span, a, blockquote
components.summary: The set of text styles a page is written in: a title, a subtitle, a paragraph, supporting text, a link and a quote. The library paints the sizes, the colours and the leading; the words and the heading levels are the host's.

components.name: Button
components.summary: An action the user takes. The one component every interface needs, and the one that has to look right in thirty-two different moods.

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: A box that either is ticked or is not, for choosing one or many things out of a list. The tick is a shape drawn in CSS, not a character.

components.name: Checkbox Group
components.summary: A set of checkboxes that share one name and belong to one field. The group is a fieldset, so the browser groups the boxes for the form and for the screen reader.

components.name: Date Picker
components.summary: A field for a date. It is a real <input type="date"> inside a box the library draws, so the browser validates the date, the arrow keys walk through it and the reader's own calendar opens it.

components.name: Field
components.summary: The scaffolding around a control: a label, the control itself, and a line of text that says what to do next. It owns the spacing, so a form does not have to.

components.name: Input / Textarea / Select
components.nameZh: 输入框 / 文本域 / 选择器
components.summary: The three text controls a form is mostly made of: a single-line input, a multi-line textarea and a native select. One stylesheet gives all three the same border, focus ring and disabled treatment, so a form reads as one form.

components.name: Input Number
components.summary: A field for a number, with a pair of buttons that step it up and down. The buttons are real buttons, so they are in the tab order and the browser announces them; the browser's own spin buttons are taken away so there is only one pair.

components.name: Radio
components.summary: A round control for choosing exactly one option out of a set. Radios that share a name form a group, and the browser owns the exclusivity.

components.name: Radio Group
components.summary: A set of radios that share one name and belong to one field. The group is a fieldset, so the browser groups the circles for the form and for the screen reader.

components.name: Rate
components.summary: A row of stars the reader sets by choosing one. The stars are real radio buttons under a drawn shape, so the value is the browser's own value and the group is the browser's own group.

components.name: Slider
components.summary: A number picked by sliding along a track. It is a native range input, so the drag, the steps and the value are the platform's.

components.name: Switch
components.summary: A binary setting that takes effect the moment it is flipped. The visible switch is drawn by the library; the control underneath it is a real checkbox.

components.name: Upload
components.summary: A file input and the list of the files that were chosen. The input is a real one, so the browser's own dialog opens and the files are chosen with the browser's own picker.

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A small picture of a person. It takes a photo, a pair of initials or an icon, and it keeps the shape of whichever mood it is in.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: A small marker that counts or names a state, attached to something else. It comes in a solid fill and a soft tint, so a page can let what matters come forward and the rest recede.

components.name: Card
components.summary: A surface that groups one thing: a title, a body, a footer. Its border, radius, shadow and fill all come from the mood, so one card reads correctly in all thirty-two of them.

components.name: Cascader
components.summary: Options in levels, opened one level at a time. Every level is a disclosure, so the browser does the opening and the closing and the state survives a reload.

components.name: Descriptions
components.summary: The facts about one thing, as label and value pairs. It is a definition list, so a screen reader announces each label before the value it belongs to.

components.name: Empty
components.summary: What a screen shows when there is nothing to show. It states the fact, and when there is a way out of it, it says what that way is.

components.name: Progress
components.summary: How much of something is done. The bar is a groove with a fill inside it, and the fill takes its width from the host.

components.name: Result
components.summary: The end of a flow: one statement of what happened, a line of explanation, and the way out. It is the whole answer on one screen, not a toast that disappears.

components.name: Skeleton
components.summary: The shape of content that has not arrived yet. Three placeholder shapes and, if the motion is welcome, a shimmer over them.

components.name: Statistic
components.summary: One number with the name of what it counts. The number is the largest thing on the block and everything else is sized around it.

components.name: Table
components.element: table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td, div
components.summary: Rows of records in columns. It is a real table, so the column names travel with the cells and a screen reader can read a row across.

components.name: Tag
components.summary: A label for one piece of data — a category, a state, a filter. The outlined member of the chip family, so it can sit beside a filled badge without either of them winning.

components.name: Timeline
components.summary: What happened, in order. An ordered list with a rail down one side and a dot at each entry, so the order is in the structure and not only in the picture.

components.name: Transfer
components.summary: Two lists side by side with a button between them: what is available on one side, what has been chosen on the other. The whole thing is a form, so the move is a submission.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.summary: The path to the page you are on, as a list of links. The separators between the steps are drawn by the stylesheet, not written into the markup as characters.

components.name: Dropdown
components.summary: A row of actions that stays out of the way until it is wanted. The trigger is a <summary>, so the panel opens and closes with the browser's own disclosure behaviour.

components.name: Menu
components.summary: A list of places to go, with groups that fold away. The groups are <details> elements, so the browser opens and closes them and keeps them open across a reload.

components.name: Pagination
components.element: nav, ul, li, a, button, input
components.summary: The pages of a long list, with the previous and next arrows at either end and the current page filled in. The arrows are chevrons drawn from two borders.

components.name: Steps
components.summary: The order of a job, one step per entry, with the step you are on picked out and the steps already done marked as finished.

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: One row of tabs over several panels of content. The tabs are radio inputs, so the browser keeps the selection, the focus and the arrow keys without a line of script.

components.name: Alert
components.summary: A message that stays in the page and says what the reader has to know: the run failed, the quota is nearly gone, the sync is through. The variant colours the border and the mark, not the text.

components.name: Loading
components.summary: A ring that turns while the library waits for something. The ring is two borders with one side left out, and the turn is a keyframe, so it needs neither a timer nor a script.

components.name: Popover
components.summary: A card that floats next to a trigger and holds more than a note: a heading, a body and a row of actions. The trigger is a <summary>, so the card opens and closes with the browser's own disclosure behaviour.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A short note that appears when the reader points at a word or tabs to it. The bubble is drawn by the stylesheet and placed with absolute positioning; the trigger is a real button, so the keyboard opens it as well as the pointer.

components.name: Divider
components.summary: A rule between two things. It can carry a label in the middle, drop the rules and keep the label, or stand up as a vertical rule.
